hold_text: Adds scripts/ops/unset_env.sh, a new system-action that mutates a live VM env file (backs it up, removes an allowlisted key's line(s)) and restarts a systemd service, plus the .github/workflows/system-actions.yml wiring that dispatches it. Per docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md's permission tiers, a runtime/service/env-mutating action is Tier-2: prepare + validate, get one operator OK in chat, then ship. This lane was asked to open the PR ready and green and report back for the operator to merge and dispatch themselves (twice, restarting ict-trader-live on the second) and verify with get-env -- so this PR does not self-land.
why: New Tier-2 system-action (unset-env) fills the gap set-env's empty-value guard deliberately leaves -- set-env can create/update an env key but, by design, can never delete one, so there was no allowlisted path to retire ARBITRATION_FANOUT_MODE / ARBITRATION_FANOUT_ACCOUNTS (both retired by E35 / #12924, issue #12938 hit the refusal trying to use set-env for this). Deletion is restricted to a fixed RETIRABLE_KEYS allowlist inside the script (starting with exactly those two keys) -- same doctrine as get_env.py::ALLOWED_KEYS -- so it can only ever remove a key someone has reviewed, never a freeform one from an issue body. Backs up the env file first (mode 600, timestamped) and removes only exact KEY= / export KEY= lines, leaving everything else byte-for-byte untouched; an absent key is a clean no-op. Also wires the action into notify_run.sh, docs/claude/system-actions.md, and tests/ops/test_system_actions_workflow.py's allowlist registries, and adds 16 new tests (positive: removal + byte-for-byte preservation + backup; negative: a non-allowlisted key is refused and the file is left untouched).
